hints: Factor out $-2$ from the quadratic and linear terms: $-2(x^2 - 4x) + 11$.
Expand the outer bracket and combine numerical terms to find $-2(x - 2)^2 + 19$, identifying vertex $(b, c) = (2, 19)$.
walkthrough:
Factor out the coefficient of $x^2$ from the terms involving $x$:
$$-2x^2 + 8x + 11 = -2(x^2 - 4x) + 11$$

Identify the integers $a = 2$, $b = 2$, $c = 19$, and state the coordinates of the vertex:
$$\text{Vertex: } (2, 19)$$

hints: Find the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points by solving $-2x^2 + 8x + 11 = 8x + 9$.
Set up the area integral $\int_{-1}^1 \left[ (-2x^2 + 8x + 11) - (8x + 9) \right] \, dx = \int_{-1}^1 (-2x^2 + 2) \, dx$ and evaluate.
walkthrough:
Find the limits of integration by equating the curve and the straight line:
$$-2x^2 + 8x + 11 = 8x + 9$$
$$-2x^2 + 2 = 0 \implies x^2 = 1 \implies x = -1, \quad x = 1$$

Subtract the line equation from the curve equation to form the area integral:
$$\text{Area} = \int_{-1}^1 \left[ (-2x^2 + 8x + 11) - (8x + 9) \right] \, dx = \int_{-1}^1 (-2x^2 + 2) \, dx$$
